shorts_extract.hook: You nod off on the living-room sofa, yet the instant your head touches the pillow your mind snaps wide awake — and reaching for a sleeping pill may silence the very pump that washes your brain.
shorts_extract.core_experiment: Xie & Nedergaard (2013) discovered brain cells shrink to widen fluid channels by 60% in deep sleep, while Fultz & Lewis (2019) filmed 20-second cerebrospinal fluid waves in sleeping humans.
shorts_extract.twist: Hauglund & Nedergaard (2025) revealed that sedative zolpidem flattens the rhythmic norepinephrine blood-vessel waves that pump fluid through the brain, trading real night washing for sedated stillness.

chapters.title: Wide Awake on the Pillow
beats: Everyday paradox: nodding off on the sofa, then snapping into alert racing thoughts the moment your head hits the bedroom pillow.
Pre-bunk the lazy advice ('just try harder to stay in bed with eyes closed') by showing why forced bed rest makes insomnia worse.
new_shots_needed: Wide moonlit walnut bedroom where a porcelain sleeper sits upright on crisp linen sheets

chapters.title: When Your Bed Becomes an Alarm
beats: Perlis & Bootzin (1997) behavioral insomnia mechanism: classical Pavlovian conditioned arousal pairs the mattress with threat vigilance and fast cortical beta waves.
Show the stimulus-control chair experiment: leaving the bed for a dim chair until eyelids droop untangles the alarm reflex.
new_shots_needed: Split-screen comparison of tossing in bed versus calm reading in a dim warm armchair

chapters.title: The 60% Emotional Disconnect
beats: Yoo & Walker (2007) fMRI study: 35 hours awake cuts the medial prefrontal brake cable and spikes amygdala emotional reactivity by 60%.
Explain why minor daytime friction feels like an emergency after a fragmented night.
new_shots_needed: 3D sagittal brain cutaway showing crimson-red hyperactive amygdala disconnected from amber-gold medial prefrontal cortex

chapters.title: The Hidden Nighttime Dishwasher
beats: Xie & Nedergaard (2013, Science): glial cells shrink during deep slow-wave sleep, widening interstitial fluid channels by 60% and flushing beta-amyloid twice as fast.
Midpoint open-loop question: if unconsciousness alone opened those channels, why don't sleeping pills wash the brain just as clean?
new_shots_needed: 3D perivascular glymphatic vessel cutaway with enclosed pearl-aqua fluid flushing amber metabolic waste

chapters.title: 20-Second Waves Inside Sleeping Humans
beats: Fultz & Lewis (2019, Science) Boston University human MRI breakthrough: synchronized delta silence, blood-volume drop, and cerebrospinal fluid surges every 20 seconds.
new_shots_needed: Widescreen clinical MRI scanner suite with porcelain researcher observing abstract fluid wave traces

chapters.title: The Sleeping-Pill Pump Paradox
beats: Hauglund & Nedergaard (2025, Cell): rhythmic 50-second locus coeruleus norepinephrine waves squeeze pial arteries like a mechanical pump during natural NREM sleep.
Zolpidem sedation mutes those norepinephrine oscillations by half and cuts brain fluid inflow by roughly one third.

chapters.title: Five Real Hours or Eight Sedated?
beats: Synthesize two evidence-backed behavioral levers (20-minute chair reset + thermal/light slow-wave priming) without preachy moralizing.
Close on the Stage 2 open-verdict forced-choice question between 5 hours of natural slow-wave sleep vs 8 sedated hours.
